newsitem.title: UK: Copper pushes higher, stocks fall again.
newsitem.headline: Copper pushes higher, stocks fall again.

text.p: Concerns over stock shortages pushed copper higher on Tuesday to fresh five-month peaks, while cocoa stumbled to near-eight month lows on widespread selling before recovering the losses.
Lead also slid to a ten-month low while nickel bounced after plunging to a two-year nadir on Monday.
Copper, the London Metal Exchange's (LME) flagship contract, spiked to fresh five-month highs after prices broke through the $2,200-a-tonne barrier in late trade on Monday.
Three months copper closed at $2,225, up $66 from Monday's finish. Traders said prices could continue to rise against the backdrop of low LME stocks.
"Copper has the potential to push higher, with stocks falling and spreads tightening," said Martin Squires of LME ring dealing member Rudolf Wolff.
"You've got to be careful with copper. It could get explosive," a copper merchant added.
Earlier LME stocks fell 5,050 tonnes to the lowest level in six years and below the 100,000-tonne threshold.
Also on the LME aluminium, used in packaging and transport, rose strongly. By 1830 GMT three month futures were nearly $50 up from Monday's close at $1,483.
Traders attributed the rise to signs that supplies may be tightening and renewed demand for metal in 1997 and 1998.

Lead, used mainly for vehicle and industrial batteries, fell to 10-month lows when funds liquidated long positions early in the day. But physical demand spurred by the cold snap in Europe helped lift the market off the lows.
Lead ended the afternoon session down $14.50 at $703, above a $693 low.
Nickel recovered from two-year lows hit on Monday, rising $240 to $6,860 amid expectations that stainless steel output, nickel's biggest market, will recover next year.
On the soft commodity markets cocoa hit their lowest level for nearly eight months at one stage before recovering to unchanged by the close in line with rising New York values.
Benchmark March cocoa hit a low of 903 stg a tonne before recovering to 913 stg by the finish.
